name: Zachary Silva
life: “I still remember a neighbor asking whether a stamp still worked on local mail.” Monday often includes a stop at the courtyard by Ferry Street Rooms, where Zachary prefers the bench where the sound of the shop door reaches before the visitor does.
voice: I was off duty and brought the letter from my neighbor to the desk. I didn't know how many people a stamp could thank.
appearance: Zachary has a strong profile and a little space between the front teeth. Look for a dark undercut with a longer wave on top. On an ordinary day, the familiar outfit is an olive canvas jacket with a folded shopping list secured by a miniature clip. In conversation Zachary squares up pieces of paper while thinking.
personality: Zachary treats keeping somebody waiting as a serious discourtesy. This can turn a helpful person into an impatient one when everybody else needs a slower conversation.
agenda: To deliver the envelope to both sets of hands.
family: Mika Williams is Zachary’s half-sibling. Zachary picks the meeting place. Mika sets the time to leave. It lets them stay close without turning a family visit into the loss of an entire day. They have both had stretches when that distinction mattered. Asked about *A last ship together*, Mika says, “I started beside a stranger and want one final day's work beside my friend even if we talk about nothing important.”
connections: Harley Dias. A neighbor handing over an envelope gives the records worker a place to send a personal reply.
